# dpttrs

> Solves a tridiagonal system of the form A·X = B using the L·D·Lᵀ factorization of A computed by DPTTRF.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dpttrs from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dpttrs';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dpttrs( order, N, nrhs, d, strideD, e, strideE, B, LDB ) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | The order of the tridiagonal matrix A.<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrix B.<br>Requires `nrhs ≥ 0` |
| `d` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | The n diagonal elements of the diagonal matrix D from the L\*D\*L\*\*T factorization of A. |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | Stride length for `d` |
| `e` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N - 1</sub> | The (n-1) subdiagonal elements of the unit bidiagonal factor L from the L\*D\*L\*\*T factorization of A. |
| ↳ `strideE` | `integer` | Stride length for `e` |
| `B` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × nrhs</sub> | **in/out** · On entry, the right hand side vectors B for the system of linear equations. On exit, the solution vectors, X. |
| ↳ `LDB` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `B`<br>Column-major requires `LDB ≥ max(1, N)`<br>Row-major requires `LDB ≥ max(1, nrhs)` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The order of the tridiagonal matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `nrhs`: The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrix B. $\mathrm{NRHS} \ge 0$.
- `d`: The n diagonal elements of the diagonal matrix D from the $L \, D \, L^T$ factorization of A.
- `e`: The (n-1) subdiagonal elements of the unit bidiagonal factor L from the $L \, D \, L^T$ factorization of A. E can also be regarded as the superdiagonal of the unit bidiagonal factor U from the factorization $A = U^T \, D \, U$.
- `B`: On entry, the right hand side vectors B for the system of linear equations. On exit, the solution vectors, X.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: info status code

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` ninth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` ninth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nrhs )` (row-major)

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dpttrs.strided(
    N, nrhs,
    d, strideD, offsetD,
    e, strideE, offsetE,
    B, strideB1, strideB2, offsetB
) → integer
```

Solves a real symmetric positive definite tridiagonal system A_X = B.
_ using the L_D*L^T factorization of A computed by dpttrf.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the tridiagonal matrix A (N >= 0)<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of right hand sides (columns of B)<br>Requires `nrhs ≥ 0` |
| `d` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Diagonal elements of D, length N |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | Stride length for `d` |
| ↳ `offsetD` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `d` |
| `e` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N - 1</sub> | Subdiagonal elements of L, length N-1 |
| ↳ `strideE` | `integer` | Stride length for `e` |
| ↳ `offsetE` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `e` |
| `B` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × nrhs</sub> | **in/out** · Right hand side matrix (N x NRHS), overwritten with solution X |
| ↳ `strideB1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `B` (row stride) |
| ↳ `strideB2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `B` (column stride) |
| ↳ `offsetB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `B` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The order of the tridiagonal matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `nrhs`: The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrix B. $\mathrm{NRHS} \ge 0$.
- `d`: The n diagonal elements of the diagonal matrix D from the $L \, D \, L^T$ factorization of A.
- `e`: The (n-1) subdiagonal elements of the unit bidiagonal factor L from the $L \, D \, L^T$ factorization of A. E can also be regarded as the superdiagonal of the unit bidiagonal factor U from the factorization $A = U^T \, D \, U$.
- `B`: On entry, the right hand side vectors B for the system of linear equations. On exit, the solution vectors, X.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0 || nrhs === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -k`, the k-th argument had an illegal value

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import discreteUniform from '@stdlib/random/array/discrete-uniform/lib/index.js';
import dpttrs from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dpttrs';

/** @type {{ dtype: 'float64' }} */
const opts = {
	'dtype': 'float64'
};
const N = 3;
const B = discreteUniform( N * N, -10, 10, opts );
const d = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );
const e = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );

// Using the standard interface:
let out = dpttrs( 'column-major', N, N, d, 1, e, 1, B, N );
console.log( out );

// Using the strided interface:
out = dpttrs.strided( N, N, d, 1, 0, e, 1, 0, B, N, 1, 0 );
console.log( out );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DPTTRS`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DPTTRS solves a tridiagonal system of the form

$$
A \, X = B
$$

using the $L \, D \, L^T$ factorization of A computed by DPTTRF. D is a diagonal matrix specified in the vector D, L is a unit bidiagonal matrix whose subdiagonal is specified in the vector E, and X and B are N by `NRHS` matrices.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
